topic.name: Writing an Infinite Geometric Series in Sigma Notation

question.text: Write the following series in sigma notation: $ - 5+ 25 - 125 + 625 - \cdots.$
question.explanation:
The first term is $a_1 = -5$ and the second term is $a_2 = 25.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

\[ r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{25}{-5} = -5 \]

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

\begin{align} a_n &= a_1\left(r\right)^{n-1} \\[5pt] &= -5\left(-5\right)^{n-1}\\[5pt] &= -5 \left(-5 \right)^{-1} \left(-5\right)^{n}\\[5pt] &=-5 \left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right) \left(-5\right)^{n}\\[5pt] &= \left(-5\right)^{n} . \end{align}

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as \begin{align*} - 5+ 25 - 125 + 625 -\cdots & = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n \\[5pt] & = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left(-5\right)^{n} . \end{align*}

example.title: Expressing an Infinite Series Using Sigma Notation Given The First Few Terms

question.text: Write the following series in sigma notation: $ 40 + 20 + 10 + 5 + \ldots .$
question.explanation:
The first term is $a_1 = 40$ and the second term is $a_2 = 20.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

\[ r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{20}{40} = \dfrac{1}{2} \]

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

\begin{align} a_n &= a_1\left(r\right)^{n-1} \\[5pt] &= 40\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1}\\[5pt] &= 40 \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{-1} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n}\\[5pt] &=40 \left(\dfrac{2}{1}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n}\\[5pt] &= 80\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n} . \end{align}

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as \begin{align*} 40 + 20 + 10 + 5 + \cdots & = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n \\[5pt] & = \sum_{n=1}^\infty 80\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n} . \end{align*}

example.title: Expressing an Infinite Series Using Sigma Notation Given The First Few Terms

question.text: Consider the infinite geometric series starting from $a_1=-14$ with the property $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=-\dfrac{1}{7}.$ Write the sum to infinity of the terms of this series using sigma notation.
question.explanation:
Notice that the sequence is a geometric sequence since the ratio of any two successive terms is constant.

The first term of the sequence is $a_1 = -14,$ and the common ratio is \[ r = \dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = -\dfrac{1}{7}. \]

Therefore, the general term $a_n$ can be expressed as

\begin{align} a_n &= a_1\left(r\right)^{n-1}\\[5pt] &= -14\left(-\dfrac{1}{7}\right)^{n-1}\\[5pt] &= -14\left(-\dfrac{1}{7} \right)^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{7}\right)^{n}\\[5pt] &= 98 \left(-\dfrac{1}{7}\right)^{n}. \end{align}

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as \begin{align*} \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n & = \sum_{n=1}^\infty 98\left(-\dfrac{1}{7}\right)^{n}. \end{align*}
